name: dev.testsy/testsy
title: Testsy
description: Run plain-English QA tests on websites and mobile apps, then inspect each check and its evidence.

tools.name: get_workspace
tools.description: The workspace this key belongs to: its id, name and plan, and this period's usage. Reference: https://testsy.dev/docs/mcp/

tools.name: get_usage
tools.description: Plan, runs used this billing period, included runs, extra-run packs and runs left. Reference: https://testsy.dev/docs/mcp/

tools.name: get_network
tools.description: How our browsers reach your sites: the static addresses to allow-list, the country they browse from, and the countries available. Reference: https://testsy.dev/docs/mcp/

tools.name: set_browse_from
tools.description: Choose the country our browsers and devices reach your sites and app servers from (web and app tests), or automatic: the site's own country (an app test then uses our default country). Reference: https://testsy.dev/docs/mcp/

tools.name: list_projects
tools.description: The projects in this workspace (a project groups the tests of one site or app). Reference: https://testsy.dev/docs/mcp/

tools.name: get_project
tools.description: One project. Reference: https://testsy.dev/docs/mcp/

tools.name: create_project
tools.description: Create a project, for example one per site or app. Reference: https://testsy.dev/docs/mcp/

tools.name: update_project
tools.description: Rename a project or change its description. Reference: https://testsy.dev/docs/mcp/

tools.name: delete_project
tools.description: Archive a project: its tests stop running; past runs stay in the run history. Reference: https://testsy.dev/docs/mcp/

tools.name: list_tests
tools.description: The tests of a project, each with its latest run. Reference: https://testsy.dev/docs/mcp/

tools.name: get_test
tools.description: One test: its start address, requirement, plan, options and latest run. Reference: https://testsy.dev/docs/mcp/

tools.name: create_test
tools.description: Create a test of a website (url) or of an app (platform android or ios, and appId; device phone or tablet and osVersion, default a phone on the latest OS). Pass `plan` (from plan_test, after the requester confirmed it): it is stored as the approved checklist and the tester follows it as written. Or pass `requirement`, plain-language text the tester plans itself at run time. Never put passwords in the text: name a sign-in account in `credentials`. Reference: https://testsy.dev/docs/mcp/

url.description: Start address (https://…); omit for app tests

requirement.description: What to do and check, in plain language (optional when plan is given)

plan.description: A plan from plan_test: {title, startUrl, steps[], checks[], record[], assumptions[], credentials[]}. Stored as the approved checklist; the tester follows it as written.

appId.description: Apps: package name or bundle id, for example com.example.app (see list_builds)

buildId.description: Apps: pin this build (ab_…); default: the app's newest build

device.description: Websites: screen, desktop (default), tablet or mobile. Apps: phone (default) or tablet — an iPhone or iPad, an Android phone or tablet (see list_devices)

osVersion.description: Apps: the OS version, latest (default) or a version — iOS: iOS 27, iOS 26, iOS 18, iOS 17; Android: Android 16, Android 15, Android 14, Android 13, Android 12, Android 11, Android 10 (see list_devices)

orientation.description: Apps: the screen's shape when the run starts — default (the device's own: phones and iPads upright, Android tablets on their side), portrait or landscape. The test may still rotate the device during the run.

credentials.description: Names of the project's sign-in accounts the tester may use (see list_credentials)

options.description: Test options, all optional: device (desktop | tablet | mobile; websites), timeoutMinutes (2-20; 20 when left out, the app sets 15), recordVideo (default true), trackers (block | allow; websites, default block), jsErrors (report | fail; websites, default report: errors from the site's own scripts are reported and fail the run only when one breaks a step; fail = any of them fails it), credentials (names of the project's sign-in accounts), services (email = its own mailbox, sms and call = its own phone number, http = the project's endpoints; sms, call and http need a paid plan), devices (1 or 2 phones; apps), platform (web | android | ios), appId and buildId (apps), buildUrl (apps: an https link to the build, downloaded every run), orientation (apps: default | portrait | landscape — the screen's shape when the run starts; default is the device's own).

tools.name: update_test
tools.description: Change a test: its title, start address, requirement, plan or options. Only the fields you pass change; within `options`, only the options you pass change and the others keep their values. Reference: https://testsy.dev/docs/mcp/

plan.description: A plan from plan_test: {title, startUrl, steps[], checks[], record[], assumptions[], credentials[]}. Stored as the approved checklist; the tester follows it as written.

osVersion.description: Apps: the OS version, latest (default) or a version — iOS: iOS 27, iOS 26, iOS 18, iOS 17; Android: Android 16, Android 15, Android 14, Android 13, Android 12, Android 11, Android 10 (see list_devices)

orientation.description: Apps: the screen's shape when the run starts — default (the device's own: phones and iPads upright, Android tablets on their side), portrait or landscape. The test may still rotate the device during the run.

options.description: Test options, all optional: device (desktop | tablet | mobile; websites), timeoutMinutes (2-20; 20 when left out, the app sets 15), recordVideo (default true), trackers (block | allow; websites, default block), jsErrors (report | fail; websites, default report: errors from the site's own scripts are reported and fail the run only when one breaks a step; fail = any of them fails it), credentials (names of the project's sign-in accounts), services (email = its own mailbox, sms and call = its own phone number, http = the project's endpoints; sms, call and http need a paid plan), devices (1 or 2 phones; apps), platform (web | android | ios), appId and buildId (apps), buildUrl (apps: an https link to the build, downloaded every run), orientation (apps: default | portrait | landscape — the screen's shape when the run starts; default is the device's own).

tools.name: duplicate_test
tools.description: Copy a test under a new title: the test's info is copied over (start address, requirement, plan, options and files). Its run history and schedules stay with the original. The copy counts toward the plan's test limit. Without `title` it is named "<original title> (copy)". Pass `projectId` to put the copy in another project of the workspace. Reference: https://testsy.dev/docs/mcp/

title.description: Title of the copy (up to 200 characters); default: the original title with " (copy)"

projectId.description: Project for the copy (p_…); default: the original's project

tools.name: delete_test
tools.description: Archive a test: it stops running; past runs stay in the run history. Reference: https://testsy.dev/docs/mcp/

tools.name: plan_test
tools.description: Have the assistant draft a test from a plain-language description, or revise a plan, without saving anything. Returns the proposed steps, checks, values to record, assumptions and any questions only the requester can answer. Show the plan to the requester; to change it, call again with `plan` and `change`; to answer questions, pass `answers`. Once they confirm, pass the plan to create_test. When no question is open the plan has passed the planning review (review.ok). Pass projectId so the assistant knows the project's sign-in accounts and endpoints. Each call uses one assistant draft of the workspace's daily allowance. Reference: https://testsy.dev/docs/mcp/

description.description: What to test, as you would brief a colleague

url.description: Start address (https://…); omit for app tests

appId.description: Apps: package name or bundle id

plan.description: A plan from an earlier plan_test call, to revise

change.description: With plan: what to change, for example "also check the price on the cart page"

answers.description: Answers to the questions of an earlier plan_test call, keyed by question id

tools.name: list_test_files
tools.description: Files a test can upload during its steps (for example an import file). Reference: https://testsy.dev/docs/mcp/

tools.name: add_test_file
tools.description: Add a file the tester can upload during the test: up to 25 MB, up to 10 files per test. REST: send the raw bytes as the body with the file name in the X-File-Name header (or ?name=), or JSON {name, contentBase64}. MCP: name and contentBase64. A file with the same name replaces the old one. Reference: https://testsy.dev/docs/mcp/

tools.name: delete_test_file
tools.description: Remove one of a test's files. Reference: https://testsy.dev/docs/mcp/

tools.name: list_credentials
tools.description: The sign-in accounts stored for a project: names, usernames and sites. Passwords are never returned. Reference: https://testsy.dev/docs/mcp/

tools.name: add_credential
tools.description: Store a sign-in account the tester can use. The password is encrypted, never returned, and never sent to the tester's AI: the tester types it. Tests refer to the account by name ("Sign in as the account \"customer\""). Through MCP the password passes through your AI agent: prefer adding passwords in the web app or over the REST API from a secret store. Reference: https://testsy.dev/docs/mcp/

name.description: Name tests use, for example customer (up to 60 characters)

tools.name: delete_credential
tools.description: Delete a sign-in account. Tests that sign in with it stop running until it is added again or they are edited. Reference: https://testsy.dev/docs/mcp/

tools.name: list_endpoints
tools.description: Calls into your own systems the tester may make during a run (for example "create a voucher"). Headers are never returned. Reference: https://testsy.dev/docs/mcp/

tools.name: add_endpoint
tools.description: Save the definition of one call into your own system that the tester may make during a run (for example "create a voucher"). This only stores the definition: it sends no request itself. The tester sees only the name, the description and what the call returned. bodyTemplate may contain {{param}} placeholders the tester fills in. Headers (for example Authorization) are encrypted and never returned. Reference: https://testsy.dev/docs/mcp/

name.description: Short name (up to 40 characters), for example create_voucher

description.description: What it does and when to use it (up to 600 characters)

tools.name: delete_endpoint
tools.description: Delete an endpoint. Reference: https://testsy.dev/docs/mcp/

tools.name: run_test
tools.description: Start a run of one test. Runs take minutes: poll get_run until final is true. watchUrl opens the run live without signing in. App tests run the newest build of their app unless buildId names another (see list_builds). watchUrl is a view-only link anyone can open (no sign-in) to watch the run live and read its result for a while after it ends; give it to the person waiting for the result. Absent when the workspace turned watch links off. REST: send an Idempotency-Key header so a retried request does not start a second run. Reference: https://testsy.dev/docs/mcp/

mode.description: auto (default) replays the learned path when it is fresh, else explores; cold always explores; warm only replays.

device.description: App tests: this run on a phone or tablet, whatever the test is set to (the test does not change; see list_devices)

osVersion.description: App tests: this run on this OS version, for example latest, iOS 26 or Android 14 (the test does not change; see list_devices)

orientation.description: App tests: this run started in this orientation, default, portrait or landscape (the test does not change)

url.description: Websites: start at this address instead of the test's saved one — a preview or staging deploy of the same site. The run then explores (cold).

tools.name: run_project
tools.description: Start a run of every test in a project (a suite). Each started run has a watchUrl to watch it live without signing in. buildIds: builds to use; each app test runs the one of its own app. Tests that could not start are listed in skipped with the reason. REST: send an Idempotency-Key header to make a retry safe. Reference: https://testsy.dev/docs/mcp/

mode.description: auto (default) replays the learned path when it is fresh, else explores; cold always explores; warm only replays.

device.description: App tests: this run on a phone or tablet, whatever the test is set to (the test does not change; see list_devices)

osVersion.description: App tests: this run on this OS version, for example latest, iOS 26 or Android 14 (the test does not change; see list_devices)

orientation.description: App tests: this run started in this orientation, default, portrait or landscape (the test does not change)

url.description: Websites: every website test starts at this address (a preview or staging deploy of the same site) and explores; app tests run their build as usual.

tools.name: list_runs
tools.description: Recent runs, newest first, optionally for one test or project or with one status; or the runs with the given ids. Reference: https://testsy.dev/docs/mcp/

ids.description: Comma-separated run ids (j_…, up to 50): returns their full views

limit.description: At most this many (default 50, up to 200)

tools.name: get_run
tools.description: A run: its status, and once final the verdict, the headline, each check's result with the reason, the values read, and links to the video, screenshots and the result page. Reference: https://testsy.dev/docs/mcp/

tools.name: wait_run
tools.description: Wait up to seconds (default 25, at most 55) for a run to finish, then return it: one call instead of polling get_run every few seconds. Call it again while final is false. The answer comes back the moment the run is final (verdict, checks and evidence in), or when the time is up with final false — then call wait_run again. Runs take 2 to 20 minutes, so expect several calls for a long run; each costs nothing while it waits. Reference: https://testsy.dev/docs/mcp/

seconds.description: How long to wait at most, 1–55 (default 25)

tools.name: stop_run
tools.description: Stop a queued or running run. A run you stop is not counted. Reference: https://testsy.dev/docs/mcp/

tools.name: create_watch_link
tools.description: A view-only link to watch a run live and read its result, with no sign-in, valid while it runs and for some hours after. Runs started here get one automatically; this makes another, or one for a run started from the web app. The link shows the live screen, the steps and checks so far, then the read-only result. membersOnly is true when the workspace limits watch links to signed-in members (or the run came from a public repository). 403 when the workspace turned watch links off. Reference: https://testsy.dev/docs/mcp/

tools.name: revoke_watch_link
tools.description: Turn off every watch link of a run straight away. Reference: https://testsy.dev/docs/mcp/

tools.name: list_share_links
tools.description: The share links made for a run, with when they expire and how often they were opened. Reference: https://testsy.dev/docs/mcp/

tools.name: create_share_link
tools.description: A read-only link to a run's result, replay and video that anyone can open without signing in, until it expires. Reference: https://testsy.dev/docs/mcp/

tools.name: delete_share_link
tools.description: Turn off a share link straight away. Reference: https://testsy.dev/docs/mcp/

tools.name: list_schedules
tools.description: When tests run by themselves: every schedule in the workspace, or those of one test or project. Reference: https://testsy.dev/docs/mcp/

tools.name: create_schedule
tools.description: Run a test by itself: on chosen weekdays, or monthly on a day, at a time in a time zone. Each scheduled run counts like any other run. Reference: https://testsy.dev/docs/mcp/

time.description: Local time, HH:MM (24 h), for example 02:00

timezone.description: IANA time zone, for example Australia/Sydney (default UTC)

tools.name: update_schedule
tools.description: Pause or resume a schedule. Reference: https://testsy.dev/docs/mcp/

enabled.description: false pauses it, true resumes it

tools.name: delete_schedule
tools.description: Delete a schedule. Reference: https://testsy.dev/docs/mcp/

tools.name: list_devices
tools.description: The phones and tablets app tests can run on, and their OS versions (latest first). Pass device and osVersion to create_test, update_test, run_test or run_project. A new app test runs on a phone with the latest OS unless you choose otherwise; the version is saved with the test, so it keeps its OS until you change it. Reference: https://testsy.dev/docs/mcp/

tools.name: list_builds
tools.description: The app builds uploaded to a project (Android .apk, iOS Simulator .app zipped), newest first, with the largest size and part size for uploads. Reference: https://testsy.dev/docs/mcp/

tools.name: get_build
tools.description: One build: its app id, version, status and any warnings. Reference: https://testsy.dev/docs/mcp/

tools.name: find_build
tools.description: Is this build already uploaded? Looks up the project's newest ready build by the file's sha256, else by a native fingerprint; build is null when neither matches. A sha256 match means the exact file is uploaded: run it with run_test {buildId} / run_project {buildIds} instead of uploading again. A fingerprint match (a hash of the native inputs the uploader stored with the build, for example @expo/fingerprint) means the native build is unchanged, so CI can skip building it. The command-line tool does this for files: testsy-ai build find / build ensure. Reference: https://testsy.dev/docs/mcp/

sha256.description: sha256 of the build file, 64 hex characters

fingerprint.description: Native fingerprint stored with the build (8–128 characters)

tools.name: create_build_upload
tools.description: Start a build upload and get signed links that upload the file without an API key: run the returned command in a shell, or PUT each part and POST complete to the links. The build is then checked and ready to run. For AI agents: tool arguments cannot carry a build, so hand the bytes to a shell command. command downloads the command-line tool and uploads the file (parts, then complete). Without it: PUT the raw bytes of part n (partBytes each, the last one shorter) to partUrlTemplate with {partNumber} replaced, then POST {parts: [{partNumber, etag}]} to completeUrl. The links expire at expiresAt and work only for this upload. Call find_build first to skip uploading a file that is already there. Reference: https://testsy.dev/docs/mcp/

label.description: A label, for example the commit (optional)

fingerprint.description: Native fingerprint to store with the build, for find_build (optional)

tools.name: import_build
tools.description: Fetch a build from an https link (an EAS, Bitrise, S3 or GitHub artifact link, up to the build size limit) into the project; it is checked and ready to run. Nothing to upload from your side. The link must be https to a public host name; up to 3 redirects are followed. headers (optional, at most 5: Authorization or X-… names) are sent to the first host only, for a private artifact store. The file name comes from Content-Disposition or the link; it must be an .apk or a zipped .app. Run the result with run_test {buildId} or run_project {buildIds}. Call find_build first when the file may already be there. Reference: https://testsy.dev/docs/mcp/

url.description: https link to the build file

headers.description: Request headers for the link, e.g. {"Authorization": "Bearer …"} (optional)

label.description: A label, for example the commit (optional)

fingerprint.description: Native fingerprint to store with the build, for find_build (optional)

tools.name: complete_build_upload
tools.description: Finish the upload with every part's etag. The build is checked (app id, version, whether our devices can run it) and returned. Use the returned build.id in run_test {buildId} or run_project {buildIds} to run the new build. Uploading alone does not start a run. The command from create_build_upload completes the upload itself; call this only after uploading parts to the signed links yourself. Also accepts the signed completeUrl instead of an API key. Reference: https://testsy.dev/docs/mcp/

tools.name: delete_build
tools.description: Delete a build. Runs that used it keep their results; a build a test pins cannot be deleted. Reference: https://testsy.dev/docs/mcp/
